note: The five flags form different contracts and cannot be cut as one unused group. The launcher inserts --interactive and --headless internally, so zero operator-typed occurrences cannot establish dead code. --no-dashboard is a documented foreground and background mode with a Remote Control safety check in AGENTS.md and the CLI reference. --logs-root was used by the isolated 2026-09-29 native Muse acceptance to keep the test run separate from the shared daemon; that is observed post-snapshot use, not evidence of frozen-period frequency. The guardrails acknowledgement is launcher-injected, and removing it changes the daemon's accepted launch contract. Consolidate internal mode handling if equivalent tests prove it; preserve the documented operator flags and safety behavior. Any line saving must be measured after implementation. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

A search that finds no `.aiurconfig` on the research host cannot measure installed users who still have one. The documented behavior deliberately rejects a legacy file with an actionable migration error, while config discovery otherwise falls through to `~/.aiur/config`. Removing that guard risks silently running a different workflow for a user who expected the local legacy file to apply. The 134-line gross estimate is too small to justify a compatibility break without a measured installed population and an equivalent fail-closed detection path. Keep the migration guard or replace it with a smaller equivalent; test local and global discovery precedence. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

`executor-fast-forward` is an exceptional repair for a wake prefix already covered by another complete means. `.claude/skills/aiur-run/SKILL.md` and the CLI reference specify owner-lease checks, exact-prefix acknowledgement and preservation of newer wakes. Zero normal invocations is expected for an emergency recovery command and does not prove the recovery path is redundant with `executor-wait`, which acknowledges only its own successful consumption. Keep the capability unless an equivalent bounded recovery route is designed and tested. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

Automatic claims and lease expiry do not replace all manual authority transitions. `.claude/skills/aiur-run/SKILL.md` treats `executor-revoke` as an operator decision after roster evidence and expressly forbids an agent from revoking a live peer itself. `executor-release` permits immediate handoff instead of waiting for TTL; claim refusal makes ownership visible. The zero-use sample is not a safe reason to remove these incident controls. Preserve them behind explicit owner/authority checks, or design and prove an equivalent takeover contract before removing a verb. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

The five commands combine an optional raw stream with persistent event-bus administration. `.claude/skills/aiur-run/SKILL.md` says `executor-listen` is optional, not obsolete, and describes `executor-emit` plus binding management for general Executor coordination; the CLI reference defines validated topic patterns. The zero invocation window does not measure all external operators or incident use. Consolidate the admin surface if the same event authority, replay, scope validation and observable receipts survive; do not delete the entire group based on a normal-loop usage count. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

The evidence does not support deleting the agent chat capability or booking an 8,500-line saving. Aiur's documented human-driven foreground mode opens a live chat pane; AGENTS.md makes real TUI chat interaction the manual acceptance path. The 2026-09-29 native Muse acceptance used that path to display a skill read, an allow-once approval, a scoped tool result and a delivered follow-up. The inherited usage sample counts mostly headless runs and has no retained pane recordings, but a missing recording is not evidence that foreground users do not use the pane. The existing bridge's private opencode SQLite dependency is a valid simplification target. A plain transcript-backed TUI can replace it only after feature parity for rendered tool/prose output, typed operator input, queued delivery, approval commands, pause/resume and restart is demonstrated in the real CLI/TUI. Count removed lines after the replacement exists and includes its tests; moving the TUI to another package is relocation, not deletion. This challenge was performed by the continuing researcher, not an independent reviewer.

The frozen delivery census shows an actual failed webhook deployment, not an unused or redundant capability. `website/docs-app/apis/github.md` documents verified-delivery gating: failed or absent deliveries keep full polling and short cache TTLs; a proven delivery widens selected reconciliation reads and retires stale cache entries. Removing ingress would delete that conditional product contract and its event latency/reconciliation path. The cited 5,721 accepted deliveries in the earlier period show a real population, while 3,524 later 502 responses show the current path needs operational diagnosis. No quota saving may be claimed during the failed period, and the proposed 5,120-line deletion is a gross estimate that omits replacement work. Keep the capability while deciding whether to repair the deployment or replace transport; test loss recovery, signature validation and measured read displacement before any cut. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

Build Order is used in the counted pack and CLI populations, and `codebase/feature-boundaries.md` assigns it a coherent domain boundary but also records tracker, catalog, dashboard and projection dependencies. The raw proposal combines a plausible package seam with unproven deletion of catalog cadence, ticket history and selected-root policy. On-demand graph reads do not automatically preserve freshness, bounded GitHub cost, recursive membership or historical context; the inherited P0 detail-loop finding also makes read policy a correctness issue. Extract a package inside the repository after its identity, event, cache and read-model contracts are characterized. Defer repository separation and any 4,000-line deletion claim until equivalent behavior and measured physical lines exist. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

The dashboard pages are a consumer of the Build Order read model, not a free-standing extraction merely because they share a name. No page-view telemetry exists, so 72 transcript URL mentions cannot measure ordinary use. The proposed collapse of PlanningSource, DataSource, SourceRuntime and ContextRuntime needs behavior tests for demo/no-source, selected root, loading, stale/error and ticket detail/history states. Keep the Phoenix presentation in the web app while moving domain reads behind an explicit contract; count any deleted lines after the replacement, not from an estimated 2,000-line collapse. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

The planning-only `aiur-build` skill declares that it prepares durable packs and never runs Aiur or implements tickets; that is a real ownership seam from the daemon. The source inventory counts actual pack directories and skill reads, so the skill is not dead. Externalize only as a separately versioned skill/plugin with its planning contract, documentation links, template loading and tests intact; ensure a later `aiur-run` can consume the same pack schema. Moving the skill to another repository removes no product complexity and creates no net LOC saving by itself. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

The frozen production code does not select `PlanningSource` through a run config, but the raw usage note missed `src/test/aiur/build_order/pack_status_test.exs`, which calls `PlanningSource.catalog/0` and `demand/1`. Cut the production demo data source only after moving those test fixtures behind the real data-source contract and preserving documentation screenshots that depend on it. The proposed 926 source lines plus bundled JSON are a gross footprint; replacement test fixture lines and any retained examples must be subtracted from a measured net deletion. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

The frozen source registers `Hooks.DomSvgLayout` in `layouts.ex:252-253` and tests its worker through a dedicated browser script, but a full `phx-hook="DomSvgLayout" search over `src` finds no mounted element. The Build Order grid uses its separate hook. That makes the ELK/DOM-SVG runtime a credible removal candidate, including its 6,312-line vendored worker, which is already over the 500-line file limit. Before deletion, search generated templates and dynamic hook names, remove the loader and packaging checks together, and run the real Build Order browser flow. Count the deleted files exactly; the raw LOC estimate omitted the worker. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

The frozen AGENTS.md explicitly claims `--debug` records each chat pane as `log/record/chat.<issue>.ansi` and keeps ANSI with `capture-pane -e`, but the source search found no recorder or stitching implementation and no retained record directory. This is a documentation defect rather than code to delete. Remove or qualify the three claims in AGENTS.md, the TUI guide and the debug skill unless the recorder is implemented and manually verified; no source-LOC saving can be booked for this cut. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

The default launcher resolves the packaged share/aiur.tmux.conf after optional AIUR_TMUX_CONF and user configuration, while scripts/verify-ctrlc-binding.sh tests scripts/aiur.tmux.conf. The two tracked copies differ materially: the test copy has synchronized-output advertising and a C-q hide binding, and the packaged copy retains the old h=...; $h form that the regression harness comment says raw-kills a pane on Ctrl+C. The source comparison is a strong defect signal, but no live packaged-keypress reproduction is claimed here. Merge the files by choosing one tested packaged source, then run the real wrapper-client keypress regression against that exact file and test C-c, C-q and user override precedence. The 109-line estimate is gross deletion only; a retained regression test and comments count toward net LOC. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

The agent-workspace --test guard blocks ticket workers from resetting pinned GitHub sandbox tickets; it does not remove Executor-root manual testing. AGENTS.md still requires the real foreground CLI/TUI smoke path, and the launcher calls preflight_stale_manual_smoke on foreground startup and reap_stale_manual_smoke on stop. The inventory uses same-user, workspace-path and tmux-aliveness checks before reaping stale BEAMs, plus orphan-attach and wrapper-socket checks. One explicit CLI use does not count automatic preflight/stop executions or the loss from abandoned child processes. Preserve scoped stale cleanup while the smoke harness exists; simplify inventory only after measuring false-positive/false-negative behavior, and keep dry-run visibility before destructive cleanup. The 181-line estimate is an unsupported net saving. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

The dispatch-budget latch is a distinct durable state. The CLI reference explicitly says resume cannot clear it, and the orchestrator has its own reset_dispatch_budget call path. Merging the spelling into `resume <id> --reset-budget` is plausible only if the implementation keeps an explicit per-ticket acknowledgement, rejects --all, preserves the latch reset transaction and documents that the flag changes two states. Do not remove the lifetime budget itself as an incidental simplification. The 35-line estimate is gross wrapper removal, not a measured net saving after parse/docs/tests. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.

The dev-only sandbox reset and timer belong beside the test fixtures rather than in the shared product launcher, but Executor-root aiurdev --test remains the canonical real CLI/TUI acceptance path in AGENTS.md; only agent-workspace launches are blocked. An extraction must preserve a one-command foreground path that starts the actual release and tmux, preserves --allow-remote safety, explicit force/clear semantics and cleanup, and keeps the user-facing CLI guide accurate. --test3 has no observed invocations in the sample, which supports prioritizing its removal after checking the three-ticket scenario owner; it does not prove that --test can be deleted. The 300-line figure is gross source movement/deletion; count retained harness lines as relocation and run manual acceptance on the extracted command. This is a continuing-researcher challenge, not an independent reviewer result.
